description: The attachment record and its migration. Stores a pointer to the file in the document store — its item identifier and a display name — never the bytes, so the document library stays the system of record for content. Belongs to exactly one pitch and records who uploaded it and when. Deleting a pitch removes its attachment rows in application code, not by a database cascade: the unit suite runs on SQLite, which does not enforce foreign keys, so a cascade would be untested here and only discovered in production.
expectedBehavior: An attachment belongs to one pitch and cannot exist without one
The record holds the store's item identifier, a display name, a content type, a size and an uploader
Deleting a pitch removes its attachment rows
The migration applies and reverses cleanly against a real Postgres
verificationSteps: Run the migration suite against a disposable Postgres and confirm upgrade and downgrade both succeed
